newsitem.title: UK: Physical Brent looks softer, outright firm.
newsitem.headline: Physical Brent looks softer, outright firm.

text.p: Little action was seen on the North Sea crude oil markets on Monday as Brent looked set to soften and the first five o' clocking of an August cargo was seen.
Outright prices soared late on Monday on short covering after news from the U.N. and rebel attacks shut down a pipeline from the Cano Limon field in Colombia.
Occidental shut in production and declared force majeure in the Cano Limon field for the second time in three weeks, a company spokesman said on Monday.
Earlier the U.N. approved a distribution plan for humanitarian supplies to Iraq, necessary before Iraq agrees to resume exporting oil.
Prices rose as traders short the prompt Brent contract on the IPE covered their requirements.
"Everyone was short and thought they would buy back when the news came out and prices went down. Prices didn't drop and they had to cover anyway," one broker said.
Physical trade on the North Sea market was confined to an end August Ekofisk at dated Brent +25 cents and an August 26 Oseberg three cents higher.
The one Brent from Monday's chains was clocked to Texaco. Many expected them to ask for a deferral from the scheduled loading date of August 19-21.
The Brent intermonth spread market was dead with no reported deals on the prompt Aug/Sept, which held strong at +35/50 cents while Sep/Oct was valued at evens and Oct/Nov -7/-5 cents.
On the Brent CFD market action was limited and concentrated on the August 11-15 week which traded at Sept +1, +2 and up to +5 cents. The August 25-29 week traded at Sept -11 cents.
On Brent a cargo due to load August 16-18 was heard offered at August evens though some claimed the market was around August -10 cents. Buying interest was muted.
